newsitem.title: UK: Dry cargo freight market holds firm.
newsitem.headline: Dry cargo freight market holds firm.

text.p: The freight market continued steady to firmer in most areas with few signs apparent yet of any softening influence from the forthcoming holidays.
The BFI added another 7 points today to 1,477 and early tonnage, especially Panamaxes, was tight in all the main loading areas.

Few caper fixtures were reported although brokers said the situation for these types was basically unchanged. Handysizes continued to enjoy buoyant demand in the Plate and Brazil, but conditions elsewhere were marginally better at best.
GRAIN - Cargill indicated the strength of the early Panamax market in the USGulf by fixing 2 handysizes on private terms in place of a Panamax for their prompt USGulf/Continent requirement.
These charterers were in the market again for a Panamax for similar business for Dec 20/Jan 6 although present indications are that the market may be no easier for these later dates.
Bestore 70,181 dwt for example, was fixed by HMM for early Jan delivery USGulf for a trip to the Far East at a firm $14,500 daily plus $285,000 bonus.

First Steamship booked the NSAC vessel National Prestige 75,000 dwt delivery prompt Immingham for 3-5 months redelivery Atlantic at a solid $12,750 daily, the first leg understood to be USGulf/Japan grain.

Meanwhile Romac conceded a strong $14,500 daily plus $280,000 bonus for the Seatrans-relet Panayia Moutsaina 68,676 dwt delivery USGulf Dec 20/24 trip Aqaba, and these charterers were understood still to have a December Panamax to fix for US Gulf/Egypt.
Continental were linked with Solidarnosc 73,470 dwt, open US Gulf about Dec 20, for grain business to Eastern Med including Israel, possibly on short period timecharter basis.

Paragon 71,200 dwt was also rumoured fixed from USGulf, possibly also by Continental, but details were not available. Another sign of the state of the Atlantic market was the rumour that Beauty Sea 69,365 dwt, reported fixed earlier this week by Interbulk delivery prompt Antwerp for 3-5 months, had been relet at $12,500 daily.
Brokers reported an acute shortage of tonnage for December loading in Argentina and Brazil and there were rumours Pioneer fixed Katya V 50,550 dwt, open Santos, for business to the Continent.

Agro-Hall booked Melodia for 20,000 Plate/Rijeka for mid Dec at $29.00, and Tradigrain fixed the 1974-built Euroliberty 29,623 dwt on subjects delivery Durban trip via Plate redelivery Skaw-Passero at $6,250 daily.

MINERALS - The fixtures of Brazil Vitoria 137,000 dwt to Golden State Delivery China early Jan for a West Australian round at $10,500 daily and Leon 145,000 dwt open China mid Dec for similar business to Trend Power at $8,400 daily both failed.
In addition the Korea Line-relet Brazil Star 211,227 dwt may have fixed and failed in the east (possibly account Navix).

Sea Gloria 157,462 dwt was rumoured fixed on private terms, also delivery far East. The strength of the South African market was shown by reports that Safmarine covered a Panamax order (possibly Saldanha/Beilun) with a small Caper on private terms.
Rumours that Cobelfret booked Obo Deniz for 120,000 coal Richards Bay to Rotterdam for Dec loading could not be confirmed.
Yukong paid up for tonnage to cover Richards Bay coal to Tarragona by booking Luise Oldendorff 72,873 dwt delivery prompt Bangkok at $9,000 daily.
The fixture of New Horizon for 60,000 coal Richards Bay/Tarragona by Carboex for Dec 20/30 at $9.70 was also reckoned by brokers to be considerably firmer.

Other Panamax news included reports of Baraganul 64,854 dwt fixed N.China/S.Korea and Global Adelaide 72,399 dwt booked for Pacific Business, but further information was lacking. In the Atlantic Cargill quoted a fresh enquiry of 55/65,000 coal Maracaibo/Ijmuiden for Dec/Jan.

HANDY-SIZES - Brokers reported that Tess-40 tonnage of 43,000 dwt had twice been fixed delivery Indian Ocean trip via Brazil to the Far East at about $9,000 daily, indicating a revival of Brazilian Steel exports.

Pisces Pioneer 35,000 dwt was said to have been fixed delivery Semarang trip via W.Australia to the far East at $7,300 daily, and the sister vessel Pisces Planter by Halla for a Nopac round in the region of a slightly firmer $7,000 daily.

Conditions for these sizes were mixed on the Continent. Moller covered a 41,000 dwt vessel to the Far East at an economical $11,300 daily, but PCL paid about $11,800 daily for the 5,000 dwt Balaji Diplomat for similar business. Taxiarhis P 35,000 dwt open Norway mid Dec was fixed on private terms.
